newsitem.title: USA: New Orleans officials say no deaths in ship crash.
newsitem.headline: New Orleans officials say no deaths in ship crash.

text.p: A freighter slammed into a crowded riverfront casino and shopping area on Saturday, but city officials said there apparently were no deaths.
New Orleans Mayor Marc Morial told a news conference rescuers were searching the rubble, but apparently no fatalities had occurred.
"We have our fingers crossed that in the end there won't be any fatalities," Morial said.
The new information contradicted earlier reports by the Coast Guard that at least six people were killed.
Earlier, Coast Guard spokesman Tyler Johnson said initial reports, though sketchy, indicated six people had died and dozens more were injured in the crash.
The New Orleans Riverwalk was heavily damaged when the Liberian-registered freighter MV Brightfield's bow slammed into the elevated strip of expensive stores overlooking the Mississippi River.
A Coast Guard spokesman said infrared scanners were being used to search for victims in the water and the rubble.
Patrons had some warning and were racing away from the waterfront when the massive ship hit the concrete seawall, crushing the walls of many stores.

The ship hit from the left side of its bow and then scraped along the seawall, finally stopping parallel to the wall. Tugs worked to hold the ship in place as rescuers searched for victims. Port of New Orleans officials said tugs were holding the ship against the seawall to help stabilise the rubble.
Television pictures showed cars buried in rubble and water from broken piping streaming down.
One witness said a strong smell of gas filled the area after the crash, causing a small panic because people worried there would be an explosion.
A three-alarm fire broke out in the shattered shopping mall shortly after the crash, a fire department spokeswoman said.

The Coast Guard said the Brightfield apparently lost power as it moved under a bridge near downtown New Orleans and hit the Riverwalk, adjacent to the downtown Hilton Hotel about 2:15 p.m. (CST) (3:15 p.m. EST) (2015 GMT).
The ship's crew were helpless to stop the vessel, but sounded a warning siren and the ship's horn repeatedly as the freighter moved inexorably toward the Riverwalk.
No injuries were reported on board the ship, which was holed and was leaking, he said.
New Orleans is one of the busiest U.S. shipping ports.
